english.title: Intercept communication - private telecommunication system - RIPA
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally, and without lawful authority, intercepted in the United Kingdom, a communication, namely **(..SPECIFY COMMUNICATION..), in the course of its transmission by means of a private telecommunication system, namely **(..SPECIFY SYSTEM..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(2) and (7) of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
intentionally
without authority
intercepted a communication in course of transmission
by means of a private telecommunication system

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required

english.notes:
(i) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required
(ii) See section 1(6) for circumstances in which conduct is excluded from criminal liability for the purposes of this offence
(iii) See section 1(5) for "conduct with lawful authority".
(iv) See section 2(2) for "intercept a communication in the course of its transmission by means of telecommunication system".
(v) See section 2(1 for definition of "private telecommunication system".

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
